extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism researchers, newsroom editors and data scientists building news-selection/homepage placement models
extracted.subtask_description: A three-dimensional operationalization for classifying news stories along topic, focus, and style (hard–soft continuum) to enable comparable measurement across studies and use as features in selection/placement models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the matter covered is politically substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: Harder topics include politics, government, policy, macroeconomy, foreign affairs, public administration. Softer topics include lifestyle, entertainment, sports (mostly), celebrity, human interest, oddities. Use topic-area content to score how 'hard' or 'soft' a story's subject is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus Dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: What aspect of the event is emphasized (societal vs. individual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harder focus emphasizes societal relevance, collective consequences, structural causes, and policy implications. Softer focus emphasizes individual/personal aspects, emotional impact, private lives, and personal experiences. Code stories on whether framing highlights public/collective consequences or personalized individual angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: How the topic is presented (tone, sourcing, structure, language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harder style: impersonal, distanced narration; technical/policy language; statistics; multiple expert sources; inverted-pyramid structure. Softer style: personalized, narrative, emotional tone; everyday vocabulary; anecdotes; single-character focus; storytelling structure. Rate style independently of topic and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-dimensional (3-vector) coding of a story
rubrics_metrics.description: Each story is coded independently on topic, focus and style producing a 3-vector rather than a binary hard/soft label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'hard news story' need not be hard on all three dimensions; a political topic may be presented in a soft style or soft focus. Use independent scores on each dimension to capture mixed/mismatch cases for analysis or model features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard Topic Bias (selection tendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets oriented toward serious/quality journalism prefer politically substantive topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operational criterion predicts topic selection biases across outlets: those with 'hard' orientation will more often select politically substantive items. Use as an explanatory variable for outlet-level placement patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soft Focus Premium
rubrics_metrics.description: Within hard topics, soft-focus framing often dominates because it satisfies engagement and personalization news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when topics are politically substantive, outlets may employ individualizing/emotional frames because they attract attention. This premium can explain prevalence of personalized stories within otherwise 'hard' beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style-Topic Mismatch as Strategic Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of applying a soft style to a hard topic as a deliberate strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: explaining policy via a single family's experience. This mixes accountability/information goals with engagement tactics; code as hard topic + soft style and treat as a distinct strategic category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trajectory Effects (temporal softening/tabloidization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Secular drift toward softer focus and style over time, often labeled 'tabloidization'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many studies show that focus and style soften over time even within elite outlets. Use longitudinal coding on the three dimensions to test which dimensions are changing (topic vs focus vs style).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet Identity Anchor
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlets brand themselves on a hard–soft profile and reproduce that identity in selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and placement reproduce an outlet's established hard/soft positioning. Use aggregate outlet-level dimension scores to model brand-based placement differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalizability for homepage/placement models
rubrics_metrics.description: A story can be scored on the three dimensions and used as features in placement-prediction or homepage-selection models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The framework is explicitly offered as directly operationalizable: include topic, focus and style scores as predictors for placement, prominence, or slot assignment on homepages and front pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prediction of placement asymmetries
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard-topic stories and soft-focus/style stories exhibit different placement patterns across page regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical expectation: hard-topic stories tend to receive higher placement on broadsheet front pages even if they have lower engagement; soft-focus/style stories dominate sidebars, lower-fold positions, and less prominent slots. Use dimension scores to predict slot-specific probabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized measurement for cross-study comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: A uniform three-dimensional coding reduces idiosyncratic codings and enables cross-national and cross-outlet comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously incompatible operationalizations hindered synthesis; adopt the standardized 3-dim scheme to compare findings across studies and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolving the 'tabloidization' debate by dimension-specific tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework allows researchers to test which specific dimensions are softening (topic, focus, or style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than treating 'tabloidization' as a single phenomenon, empirically distinguish whether change is driven by topic shifts, personalization of focus, stylistic changes, or combinations thereof.
